quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: You hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the parked vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the parked vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked vehicle or property, you must leave a note with your name, phone number, and address on the vehicle or property you hit.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow traffic light, you should:

options.text: Treat the light like a stop sign.
Wait until the light turns green to proceed.
Slow down and go through the intersection carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and go through the intersection carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution. You do not need to stop unless it is unsafe to proceed.

questions.question: Your rearview mirror should be adjusted so you can see:

options.text: The entire rear window.
The passengers in the backseat.
Your own reflection.

questions.correctAnswerText: The entire rear window.
questions.explanation: Adjust your inside rearview mirror so you can see the entire rear window from the driver's seat. You should only move your eyes, not your head, to use this mirror.

questions.question: You are driving behind a motorcycle and want to pass. You must:

options.text: Stay in the right lane because the motorcycle is small and does not use all of the lane.
Blow your horn to make the motorcycle move to the shoulder.
Have your entire vehicle in the left lane before and during the pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have your entire vehicle in the left lane before and during the pass.
questions.explanation: Allow a full lane to the motorcycle when passing. Never share the same lane as a motorcycle. Returning to the original lane too soon can force the rider to swerve right into traffic or off the road.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Change lanes suddenly without warning.
Check for other vehicles in the lane you want to enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes suddenly without warning.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, check your mirrors and blind spots for other vehicles. Always use your turn signal before changing lanes to warn other drivers.

questions.question: Which describes how defensive drivers think?

options.text: They know other drivers will do the right thing.
They think about what other drivers might do and prepare to react.
They expect no mercy and give none.

questions.correctAnswerText: They think about what other drivers might do and prepare to react.
questions.explanation: Defensive drivers expect mistakes from other drivers and prepare to react to prevent accidents.

questions.question: What can happen if you take a prescription drug and drink alcohol?

options.text: There will be no effect.
You will be more alert.
You may not be safe to drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not be safe to drive.
questions.explanation: Both prescription and over-the-counter medicines can affect your driving ability. They are especially dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: You may cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle if the:

options.text: Vehicle in front of you moves to the right to let you pass.
Yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
Yellow line on the opposite side of the road is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on your side means you may pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: You must always stop before crossing railroad tracks when:

options.text: You cannot completely cross the tracks before having to stop.
The crossing is in a town with frequent train traffic.
You are carrying two or more young children.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot completely cross the tracks before having to stop.
questions.explanation: Expect a train at any time on any track. Make sure your vehicle completely clears the tracks before you stop.

questions.question: This yellow sign means:

options.text: There is a sharp turn to the right.
The lane must turn right.
You can only turn right on a green arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a sharp turn to the right.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert you to upcoming road conditions like sharp turns and curves.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Side road.
Merge.
Yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Side road.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a side road is coming ahead.

questions.question: To check your blind spot when changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Only check the left outside mirror.
Look over your left or right shoulder.
Only check the inside rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your left or right shoulder.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check these areas before changing lanes.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection at the speed limit when the light turns yellow. You should:

options.text: Slow down and go through without worrying.
Speed up to cross before the light turns red.
Stop before entering the intersection, if you can do so safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection, if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming. Stop if you can do so safely. Otherwise, cross the intersection carefully.

questions.question: You have a green light and there are pedestrians in the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: You must let pedestrians cross first.
You have the right to go before pedestrians.
Pedestrians must wait for you to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must let pedestrians cross first.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, you must yield to pedestrians already in the intersection. This includes when you are turning.

questions.question: A truck or bus is turning right, and you also need to turn right. What should you do?

options.text: Turn quickly before the truck or bus does.
Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning.
Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning.
questions.explanation: Do not try to fit between a turning truck or bus and the curb. This can cause a serious crash. Wait for the truck or bus to complete its turn before you turn.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: You can pass from the lane with the solid yellow line.
No one can pass from either lane.
You can pass from the lane with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from the lane with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means you can pass. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. When they are together, only the lane with the broken line can pass.

questions.question: When turning left, who must you yield to?

options.text: Oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right.
Passing cars.
No one in particular.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to all vehicles coming toward you. This includes cars, bicycles, and motorcycles.

questions.question: What should you do when driving near a large truck or bus?

options.text: Follow it closely to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.
Avoid driving beside it for long periods.
Drive on its right side on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving beside it for long periods.
questions.explanation: Large trucks and buses have large blind spots on both sides. Do not stay beside them for a long time.

questions.question: An oncoming vehicle has its high beams on and you cannot see the road. What should you do?

options.text: Look toward the left edge of your lane.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.
Look straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at the bright headlights. Instead, look at the right edge of your lane and watch the oncoming vehicle from the corner of your eye.

questions.question: Bad suspension can cause:

options.text: Loss of control of your vehicle.
Squealing brakes.
Loose steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Loss of control of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Suspension helps control your vehicle and gives a smooth ride. If your car bounces a lot after bumps or is hard to control, you may need new suspension parts.

questions.question: You are tired while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Drive faster to reach your destination sooner.
Turn up your radio volume.
Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.
questions.explanation: If you are struggling to keep your eyes open, drifting out of your lane, or using tricks like loud radio to stay awake, you are too tired to drive. Stop and rest at a safe location.

questions.question: You want to pass a pedestrian walking on the road, but an oncoming vehicle is coming. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first.
Keep going at the same speed. The oncoming vehicle must stop.
Honk to tell the pedestrian to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass. Then pass the pedestrian if it is safe.

questions.question: You are stopped for a train at a railroad crossing. After the train passes, what should you do?

options.text: Wait for the signal lights to stop flashing.
Check for a second train.
Do both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do both of the above.
questions.explanation: After a train passes, another train may be coming on another track. Wait until all gates are raised and all warning lights stop flashing before you proceed.

questions.question: Can you pass another vehicle by driving on the shoulder?

options.text: Yes, if the shoulder is paved.
Yes, if the other vehicle is turning left.
No, never.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: Never pass by using the shoulder of the road. Other drivers do not expect you there and may pull onto the shoulder without looking.

questions.question: You have a minor crash at an intersection with no injuries and little damage. What should you do?

options.text: Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until police arrive.
Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if you can.
Do not move your vehicle for any reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if you can.
questions.explanation: If no one is hurt or killed and it is safe, move your vehicle out of the traffic lane.
